title: Cash-flow valuation declares the first observation time
question: A first flow at t=0 differs from t=1; scheduled durations also require a declared calendar/time basis.

evidence.title: Discounting requires an explicit first-cash-flow time
explanation: Periodic NPV discounts its first flow at period1; scheduled NPV anchors the first supplied date at0 and divides signed elapsed hours by24 and365.
The loops use i versus dates[i-1]-dates[0]; the difference is explicit source policy and not interchangeable naming.

evidence.title: State, transition and certain channels have different current-time inclusion
explanation: State cashflows exist at every grid date, transitions at stop dates after the first; incoming transitions are settled in before/after observations. Certain payments include or exclude equality explicitly and are valued beyond the grid from their own dates; certain-only valuation skips model traversal. Terminal values apply once to state/transition components, never to certain payments.
Engine-source mechanisms only; FinanceCore discount implementation and consumer mortality model remain pending, so financial valuation correctness is not asserted.

evidence.title: Annualized annuities separate installment size, timing and guarantee
explanation: Annuities pay1/frequency perinstallment. Due versus Immediate shifts first date by one period; start_time defers commencement. Guaranteed installments begin atcommencement and can survive death atissue or during deferral; contingent installments depend on observed active state. Termzero is empty; positive integer frequency and nonnegative whole guarantee/start/term controls are explicit.
Source-defined unit products only, excluding expense, profit and statutory reserve policies. Stored expected payment and PV identities are source-read, never executed.

evidence.title: Product settlement phase and near-date snapping are explicit valuation policy
explanation: End-period death/immediate payments are settled at valuation date; due-before keeps the installment atthat date and after settles it. Product APIs differ from raw engine before/after-every-state-payment phases. Query time snaps only within max(1e-9/frequency,4ulps) and below half-period distance; known-state death/endowment valuation otherwise requires integer anniversary. Premium subperiod refinement retains year-end death settlement through interval discount factors.
Snapping is floating time policy, not exact Money comparison. Source regression assertions were read but never executed; curve correctness and timing applicability depend on caller context.
